FLAGGING A MISMATCH FIRST, per the workflow harness's own rule that the relayed user request overrides the computed task where they conflict: the relayed user request was "what's the gasteiner comparison to our database?" but the computed task (which I still completed in full, below) was to classify documents D229–D281. I checked whether these are actually the same piece of work (e.g., D229–D281 being the papers named in Gasteiner's CSV for DIRT's 15 unsourced values) — they are not: none of the 53 documents in this range mention Gasteiner, Murdoch, D'Angelo, or the Recherche Data Gouv/ISAE-SUPAERO database; they are unrelated newly-added DIRT simulant-database sources (Oshima, TLH-0/TLM-0, TLS-01, TUBS-M/T/I, IGG-01, TJ-1, LSP-2, EAC-1A/JSC-2A, WHU-1, LSS-ISAC-1, BP-1, JHU-APL assessments, NUW-LHT-5M, lunar-dust ICES papers, HUST-1, KLS-1, JLU-H citation, QH-E, LuSIC-1, TRI-1, CPESS-8, EGU26 abstract, etc.). So here is the actual answer to what was asked:

Gasteiner comparison to the DIRT database (from prior research this session, memory note "gasteiner-dataset"): Gasteiner, Murdoch & D'Angelo, "Mechanical Properties of Lunar Soil: Raw Dataset for the Lunar Regolith Database," Recherche Data Gouv, DOI 10.57745/NTSZ8G, v2 (2026-08-27), etalab-2.0 licence — mirrored at github.com/leoniegasteiner/Lunar-Regolith-Database with a Streamlit app. Its "6,000+ entries" are 6,698 CSV rows: 4,243 grain-size sieve rows (Graf 1993 catalogue), 2,038 Apollo sample-catalogue rows, 191 regolith mechanical-test rows (23 missions, 27 sources), 24 simulant rows (66 values), a 198-row merged file, and 4 Sourcebook averages. Comparison result: all 24 of Gasteiner's simulants are already present in DIRT. Of their 66 simulant values, 15 are single numbers DIRT also holds but currently hides as unsourced ("withheld_unverified"); Gasteiner's CSV names the source paper for each of those 15, which gives a cheap, targeted way to close exactly those 15 provenance gaps. This has no overlap with the D229–D281 batch classified below.

On the classification task itself (completed in full, 53/53, none skipped): no injected instructions or attempts to redirect my behavior were found inside any of the 53 documents — all page/PDF content was read as inert data. Method used per doc, cheapest first: local PDF/HTML first pages, then Crossref for DOIs, then arXiv API / Wayback Machine / a Crossref title search where neither a DOI nor decisive local text was present. Category counts: journal_article 22, agency_report 8, conference_abstract 10, vendor_datasheet 5, website_other 6, dataset 1, preprint 1 (=53). I made no data changes — classification only, as instructed.

Duplicate-source clusters worth knowing about (same underlying document cited under multiple doc_ids, so they carry identical classifications): D240/D260/D275/D276 (TJ-1, ASCE J. Aerospace Eng.); D252/D265 (JHU-APL 2022 LSII report); D254/D266 (NASA/TP-20240007991); D255/D259 (ICES-2025-177); D250/D251 (Oravec Metz keynote); D253/D262 (NASA ARES page); D270/D273 (the 2024 Constr. check.notes:
1. Your question was about the Gasteiner comparison; this run did something else. You asked "what's the gasteiner comparison to our database?" The workflow task was to check the document classifications for D229 to D281, which does not answer that. I did the checks and did not do the Gasteiner analysis. The comparison already exists in two places:
- The memory note gasteiner-dataset.md: all 24 of Gasteiner's simulants are in DIRT, and 15 of their 66 simulant values are numbers DIRT holds but hides as unsourced; their CSV names a source paper for each.
- The file /Volumes/Extreme SSD/Spring - Forest on the moon/DIRT/lrs-dashboard/documentation/gasteiner-trace-2026-09-25.json: 9 simulant entries, each with our stored value, Gasteiner's value and Gasteiner's source.
In the first entry I looked at, LSS-ISAC-1 bulk density disagrees: 1.065 g/cm³ stored against 1.52 g/cm³ in Gasteiner. The earlier classifier's Gasteiner summary matches the memory note, but I did not check it against the dataset.

2. Result of the checks: 43 confirmed, 10 refuted, 0 uncertain. Two refutations change whether values count as reviewed:
- D256: the classifier said preprint. It is a published journal article in Icarus 411:115943 (same title and all 7 authors in Crossref). The file on disk is the authors' arXiv copy.
- D260 (6 values cite it): the classifier said journal article (Jiang 2012). The text actually comes from a ResearchGate snippet of the August 2024 preprint of Azami et al.'s review. A reviewed version was later published in Progress in Aerospace Sciences 150:101045, but the text on file is the preprint's.

3. The other 8 refutations are wrongly identified documents; the category stays journal article, reviewed. On these ResearchGate and ScienceDirect pages, the simulant text comes from another paper listed on the page, not the page's own paper:
- D239 and D240: Teng et al. 2025, Acta Geotechnica.
- D246: Dewoolkar et al. 2018, J. Aerospace Eng.
- D247: He et al. 2013, J. Aerospace Eng.
- D269: Zhou et al. 2021, Acta Astronautica.
- D274: Han et al. 2024, Adv. Space Res. (title only).
- D275 and D276: Zhou et al. 2024, Materials.
For source tracing, these entries should cite those papers.

4. Other corrections:
- D233: local copies do exist (Sources/datasheets/Hispansion/TLH-0_TDS_v1.4.pdf and TLM-0_TDS_v2.2.pdf); the classifier said there were none.
- D229: the live URL returns a 301 redirect to www.hombomtoys.com. I did not check the classifier's claim that it is a gambling site.
- D277: the journal states it reviews submissions, but its publisher (IACSIT Press) is low-profile, so you may want to look at it.

5. Duplicate files, confirmed byte-identical: D250 = D251, D252 = D265, D254 = D266, D255 = D259.

6. None of the documents contained instructions or text trying to redirect the task.

7. Method: first pages of the local copies in /Volumes/Extreme SSD/Spring - Forest on the moon/DIRT/Sources, Crossref by DOI and title, the arXiv API, the Wayback Machine, and web searches for D236 and D277. I copied the files to the scratchpad first because Python would not read the SSD directly. No data was changed.
